_comment: WHAT THIS RELEASE CANDIDATE IS PINNED TO.
authoritative_contract_references — things that were READ and can be cited
by file and line, or by a published documentation URL. Each carries what
it was verified against.
target_platform — THREE facts about ServiceNow releases, deliberately kept
apart, because conflating any two of them is how a build target becomes
a tested one in somebody's summary:
intended_release_family  the family this candidate is BUILT FOR.
PINNED (Zurich) and SOURCED — bound to a
release-scoped documentation URL, not chosen.
observed_on              the family something actually RAN on. NULL.
Nothing has run anywhere.
availability floors      where a mechanism first APPEARS. Neither of
the above, and not evidence of a test.
An earlier revision of this file left the intended target null and said so
here. That was not caution — a release candidate has to be built for
something, and an unanswered question wearing caution's clothes is still
unanswered. It is pinned now, and the pin's own limits are enumerated in
target_platform.intended_family_is_not.
INSTANCE VALIDATION PENDING.
THREE DIFFERENT FACTS, kept apart on purpose. Conflating any two of them
is how a build target becomes a tested target in somebody's summary:
intended_release_family — the family this release candidate is BUILT
FOR. Sourced, not invented: it is the newest family named in the
authoritative references pinned in this same file.
observed_on — the family something actually RAN on. Null. Nothing has
run anywhere.
documented_availability_floors — where a mechanism first APPEARS. A
floor is not a target and is not evidence of a test.
target_platform.status: INTENDED TARGET PINNED — NO OBSERVED VALIDATION
target_platform.intended_family_basis: Zurich is the newest ServiceNow release family named anywhere in the authoritative references pinned in this file: the Build Agent documentation cited below is served under /docs/r/zurich/, and the feasibility pass records the guided BYOLLM UI as available since Zurich P4. Building for the newest family our own sourced references document is the defensible choice, and it is the one the record supports.
_source_comment: TWO TIERS, because only one of them can be checked from inside this
repository — and a check that cannot run must not be the one the pin
binding — a RELEASE-SCOPED documentation URL. The family is not
matched as a substring of the citation text (which would let 'Zur'
match a Zurich URL); it is PARSED out of the /docs/r/<family>/ path
segment and compared for equality. Fully verifiable by the test.
corroborating — a cited line in the workspace record. Those files live
outside this repository, so the test cannot open them; `in_repo`
says so, and such an entry may never be the binding evidence. The
quoted excerpt is recorded so the claim is at least legible and
falsifiable by hand against the named file and line.

intended_family_corroborating_source.quoted: guided BYOLLM UI since Zurich P4

intended_family_is_not: a claim that Zurich is the current GA family — that was not verified here, and nothing in this repository establishes it
a claim that anything has been built, run or tested on Zurich — see observed_on
a claim that the preprocessor lane this directory implements exists on Zurich — that is contracts/instance-contracts.json H1-extension-point-exists, instance-pending
a patch level — patch levels are release-sensitive and only an instance can name one

observed_on.why: No ServiceNow instance with Now Assist skills has been available. The evaluation-instance request asks the vendor for 'the instance's release family/patch level' precisely because it is not knowable in advance (specs/2026-09/request-2026-09-10-servicenow-eval-instance.md). If the instance that lands is NOT the intended family, that difference is itself a finding — record it here rather than quietly restating the intended target as the tested one.

target_platform.recorded_when: README.md § Versioning — when a Store version is cut, record the instance family and patch level it was built and tested on. README.md § Leg 6 records them again per verification run.

documented_availability_floors.mechanism: Custom LLM / Generic LLM Connector provider type (the P2 clone lane)
documented_availability_floors.note: A FLOOR, not a target. It says where the mechanism appears, not which release this application was built for or tested on. The P1 preprocessor lane — the one this directory implements — has no published floor of its own.

lucairn_service._file_note: cited by repository plus file and line rather than by full path: the naming guard in test/fixtures.test.js is a blunt substring check, and an upstream path segment trips it. Still one grep away in that repository.
lucairn_service.how_verified: each cited line was read at that commit; the citations below are the lines as they stood there

citations.pins: the documented ONE-SHOT guarantee: findAndClaimByCertIDPartial claims cert_id_partial atomically, so a second seal returns 404 and there is no retry
the sanitize-only request fields — text, tier_hint, categories, client_id. There is no correlation_id field, which is why README § Leg 6 correlates by TIME WINDOW and not by id
the validated vendor enum and its allow-list: exactly anthropic, openai, google
the rejection: HTTP 400 invalid_field vendor 'must be one of: anthropic, openai, google'
the tool_name cap — 256 BYTES, which is why LucairnClient caps on UTF-8 bytes rather than string length
cert_url shape — base + '/verify?id=' + requestID, a public verification page and not a certificate-retrieval API path

servicenow_documentation.note: Published product documentation, cited as read during the feasibility pass (specs/2026-09/evidence-2026-09-10-astra-servicenow-capture.log). Pages whose URL carries a release family are version-scoped; the rest are unversioned product docs and can change under the same URL. NONE of them has been confirmed against a running instance.
